note: Static analysis only (no compilation, no test execution) per skill. Segment root is backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ (the skill's segment-map path backend/api-server/src/handlers/ is stale for this repo layout; the real api-handlers surface is routes/ = 203 files / ~135k LOC). Per the skill's >40-file rule the review narrowed to a cross-cutting security+Rust grep sweep and then read only the hit sites plus the largest/recently-touched files. This is an EXCEPTIONALLY hardened segment and almost every pattern scanned came up CLEAN this pass (recorded so future rotations do not re-mine speculatively): (a) SECRET-IN-LOG (CWE-532) — every tracing:: hit over password/secret/token/api_key logs only `error = %e` or `user_id`, never a credential value; the 'token' matches are the nouns 'verification token'/'reset token' in messages, not values. (b) CORS AllowAny / mirror_request — none in routes. (c) todo!()/unimplemented!() in production handler paths — none. (d) SHELL/PATH INJECTION — no Command::new / process; the format!("/...") hits are all URL-path builders over Uuid/opaque tokens, not filesystem paths. (e) UNWRAP/EXPECT crash paths — only 13 non-test unwrap/expect in all 203 route files, and NONE touch DB/parse/header/json; each is either an infallible literal (and_hms_opt on 00:00:00 / 23:59:59, HMAC new_from_slice 'accepts any key length'), a startup-validated secret (ESIGN_TOKEN_SECRET), a guarded `x.is_none() || x.as_ref().unwrap()` short-circuit (lease_abstraction, agencies), an OS-rng expect, or a documented mutex-poison expect (oauth_state). (f) TENANT-SCOPING / IDOR — the direct sqlx::query sites are exemplary: non-admin routes consistently bind rls.tenant_id()/org_id/user_id and carry explicit 'Critical 1.1/1.4 IDOR guard' comments (messaging, voting, neighbors, documents/shares, work_orders verify_org_access); the un-scoped aggregate queries in compliance.rs (COUNT(*) FROM users ...) are all behind require_platform_admin(&user)? so platform-wide totals are intentional; gdpr.rs update_privacy_settings UPDATE ... WHERE id=$3 binds the caller's own user.user_id (self-scoped, no IDOR). (g) RATE-LIMITING — resend-verification, password_reset, registration, mfa, document shares all carry throttles. (h) voice_webhooks device auth is defence-in-depth (keyed-HMAC narrow + AES-GCM decrypt + constant-time verify as the authority). The one genuine net-new defect is below: verify_email consumes the single-use token non-atomically and swallows the consume error, so the single-use guarantee can be silently defeated and a transient DB error can burn an otherwise-valid link. Net-new: grep of .research/backlog.json for verify-email / verification-token / use_verification_token returned nothing, and it is not among the 2026-10-01 api-core signals.

evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth/registration.rs:276-311 — verify_email() consumes the email-verification token non-atomically and in the wrong order. It first calls use_verification_token(id) to mark the token used, but the Result is SWALLOWED: `if let Err(e) = state.user_repo.use_verification_token(...).await { tracing::error!(error = %e, "Failed to mark verification token as used"); }` — logged, NO early return — then it proceeds to verify_email(user_id).

Consequence 1 (single-use guarantee silently defeated): use_verification_token issues `UPDATE email_verification_tokens SET used_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1 AND used_at IS NULL` (backend/crates/db/src/repositories/user.rs:305-312) and lookup is `SELECT * FROM email_verification_tokens WHERE token_hash = $1 AND used_at IS NULL` (user.rs:287-295). If the UPDATE errors (DB blip / transient failure) the error is dropped, used_at stays NULL, and the token REMAINS VALID and REPLAYABLE on the public unauthenticated GET /api/v1/auth/verify-email endpoint. The replay impact is bounded (email verification is idempotent: a second verify_email returns Ok(None) -> 'already verified'), which is why this is Low rather than High — but a verification link that is supposed to be strictly single-use is not, and the defeat is silent.

Consequence 2 (consume-before-verify burns valid links): because the token is marked used BEFORE verify_email() runs, if verify_email() returns Err (its own DB error, handled at :303-308) the link has already been consumed (used_at set) while the email is still unverified — the user's link is burned and they must request a fresh one for a failure that had nothing to do with the token.

Net-new + landable remedy (backend-only, confined to verify_email): make the consume authoritative and ordered — either (a) treat a use_verification_token Err as a hard failure (return 500 instead of swallowing) AND mark-used only after verify_email succeeds, or (b) better, fold mark-used + verify_email into one transaction so the token is consumed iff verification commits, closing both the replay window and the burned-link window. Verifiable via `cargo build -p api-server` + a unit test asserting (i) used_at is set only on successful verify and (ii) a failing consume does not leave the token replayable. Confidence medium: the swallow and the ordering are confirmed by static read of both the handler and the repo SQL; the trigger is a transient DB error, so it is latent rather than runtime-confirmed.
